profileEvidence.author: A
profileEvidence.summary: Good-natured, affectionate and lively, Paisley Terriers were prized as companions. They could kill rats, but were chiefly kept as pets. Fanciers in the Clyde valley built a following for this silky-coated variety, and separate show classes helped distinguish it from the hard-coated Skye Terrier.
profileEvidence.shortDescription: Lively and affectionate, Paisley Terriers belonged to a Scottish companion tradition that found its own place on the show bench.
